messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High GPU queue growth detected in hosted-eu-north (pool=GPU-NE-1). Provisioner heartbeat missed repeatedly (provisioner=prov-eu-1). Queue depth: 4.2k pending requests; p95 latency 12.1s (baseline 0.3s); p99 latency 27.8s. 504 timeout rate up 8x. Control plane shows failed scale attempts. Runbook: https://intranet/runbooks/gpu-provisioner-heartbeat
alicia: ack. I'm oncall. Paging infra and runtime. Seeing synthetic probes spike at 18:20 UTC. Putting this thread as primary comms.
ben: on my way. hitting the provisioner logs now. Cloud provider returning 429/503 on instance create calls. Auto-scale attempts are getting rate-limited by provider. Also seeing attach timeouts.
carol: confirmed. provisioner pod logs: "Leader lost heartbeat to control-plane", repeated "AttachError: Timeout while attaching GPU". Many scale jobs stuck in PENDING for >4m.
alicia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply fallback routing to lower-cost quantized variant in eu-west to shed pressure on eu-north GPUs; 2) enable temporary rate limits for non-paid tiers; 3) try restart of provisioner after reroute. Ben, can you apply routing change?
ben: applying now — curl posted to internal routing API: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routes -d '{"from_region":"eu-north","fallback":"model_v1_q4","weight":0.8}'` -> 200 OK. Starting traffic shift (80% to model_v1_q4).
deploy-bot: Canary route applied. 80% traffic to model_v1_q4 in eu-west. Observability will report metrics in ~30s.
ops-manager: also enabling global rate limit for free-tier to 5rps to reduce churn (applied via rate-limit service). Notifying growth/marketing.
ben: infra update: cloud quota for GPU type (g5.xlarge equivalent) exhausted in eu-north. Opened emergency quota request with provider (req=REQ-xyz-123). Provider response ETA unknown.
carol: with quota blocked, provisioner can't bring up new nodes. Suggest regional failover if quota won't be cleared quickly. We can shift more traffic to eu-west/us-west — tradeoff is higher network latency for EU customers but preserves availability.
alicia: agree. Ben, initiate cross-region shift to eu-west (60%) and us-west (40%) while we wait on quota. Use force mode.
ben: running route-shift: `./tools/route-shift --from eu-north --to eu-west,us-west --ratio 0.6,0.4 --force` -> started. Expect 5-10m of extra tail latency for some EU customers during TLS handoffs.
prod-support: heads-up sent to account reps for potentially impacted customers (ids: CUST-12, CUST-47, CUST-88). Draft notification in #customer-notify for review: "You may see increased latency or errors for ~20-40 minutes while we mitigate." 
incident-bot: metrics: queue depth plateauing, now slowly decreasing from 4.2k -> 1.8k over 6m. p95 dropping from 12.1s -> 3.5s. 504 rate improving but still elevated.
carol: provisioning still unstable. I'm restarting provisioner pods in eu-north: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/provisioner-eu-1` -> restart triggered.
ben: restart finished. New provisioner leader elected. Provisioner is now issuing attach calls again, but some attach calls still timing out. Cloud API backoff in effect (429s) causing slow node creation.
alicia: while node attach continues, let's warm model caches to reduce token re-generation. Carol, can you prime the KV cache for model_v2 and model_v1_q4 common prefixes?
carol: priming started: `./prime-cache --model model_v2 --keys top_10k && ./prime-cache --model model_v1_q4 --keys top_5k` -> running in background.
ops-manager: quick customer-impact estimate: ~12 customers saw >1% error increase; 3 customers saw >5% errors during peak. Window of notable impact: 18:21 -> 19:03 UTC. Estimated SLO exposure: p99 latency breach for ~40 minutes. Flagging finance/ops for potential credits.
prod-support: proposing proactive credits for affected enterprise customers. Draft: "We're investigating an infrastructure outage causing increased timeouts; working on mitigation; we'll follow up with root cause and credits if warranted." Please review in #customer-notify.
alicia: handoff to night shift in 30m. @dave you'll be lead going forward. Current status and actions completed: traffic rerouted to fallback model, global rate-limit applied, provisioner restarted, cache priming in progress.
dave: ack — taking over. I'll monitor provisioning attach success (need 6 new GPU nodes to be healthy) and keep vendor ticket open. Please ping me if anything else flares.
ben: note: cloud vendor says quota increase may be slow. We're exploring temporary multi-tenant oversubscription for non-sensitive workloads as a last resort (requires ops signoff).
carol: logs snippet for triage (posted to GCS): ```
2026-05-12T18:19:42Z provisioner-eu-1 ERROR LeaderLost: heartbeat timeout to control-plane
2026-05-12T18:20:11Z provisioner-eu-1 ERROR AttachError: Timeout while attaching GPU nvme-controller to instance i-0abcde
2026-05-12T18:21:02Z autoscaler INFO ScaleAttempt job=scale-789 status=PENDING reason=ProviderQuota
```
alicia: created incident ticket INC-2026-045, priority P1. Postmortem owner assigned: carol. Postmortem link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-045
incident-bot: Severity update: elevated to Sev2 due to SLO exposure. Notifications sent to execs and SRE lead.
ben: remaining action items for night: 1) confirm 6 GPUs attached & healthy; 2) verify 504/error rate back to baseline <1%; 3) follow up with cloud vendor quota (REQ-xyz-123). I'll keep tab on console.
carol: I'll draft initial RCA notes on provisioner leader election + provider quota interplay. Will include mitigation runbook updates (add faster regional failover steps + circuit-breaker on scale attempts).
alicia: thanks team. Closing live mitigation phase for now. If anything regresses, page @dave directly. We'll assemble postmortem and customer impact summary in #postmortems.
dave: noted. Monitoring interval set to 1m. Leaving a watch window until 21:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident closed for live ops (mitigation successful). Postmortem assigned. Reaction: :white_check_mark:
